_why: ONE fixture, parsed by BOTH halves of the scrubber rail's Rust->TS seam (bead sparkle-7m719).
The Rust suite asserts that serde's derive produces exactly these objects for PromptMarker and
RangeRow (src-tauri/src/history.rs); the TypeScript suite asserts that PromptMarkerRow and
HistoryRangeRow (src/services/history.ts) read exactly these keys. A field renamed on one side
reds a test on BOTH, which is the point: two green suites either side of a wire that disagrees
is the measured way a feature ships completely inert (AGENTS.md, 'A Rust Option crosses the
wire as null'). Every field here is non-optional by construction, so there is no null case.
The ids look like concierge message ids on purpose: for source='concierge' the history row id
IS the message id, which is what lets the rail scroll the thread to a specific bubble.
SECOND WAVE (bead sparkle-bjbhw6, defects 3 and 7): historyExtent / historyExtentEmpty for the
scope menu's true extent, and promptBucket for the bucketed density the rail is DRAWN from. The
version stays 1 — these are additive keys, and no existing key moved.
historyExtentEmpty is the only fixture here carrying nulls, and it is the whole reason it exists:
HistoryExtent's two bounds are Rust Options, an Option crosses the wire as an EXPLICIT null and
never as an absent key, so the TS side must read `oldestMs: number | null`. `oldestMs?: number`
is number|undefined, which excludes null — a parser describing a payload the wire cannot make.
